item.title: DasherControl: a homelab dashboard built around workspaces
item.description: I started DasherControl because my homelab services kept spreading across browser tabs. The idea was a workspace of applets: bookmarks and embedded applications arranged in a dashboard, with a few Docker controls nearby.

item.title: MediaBox homelab — what I run in Docker (and what stayed a bookmark)
item.description: I kept a private list of self-hosted apps I wanted to try — mostly so I would stop assigning random ports and forgetting what lived on :8096. That list turned into MediaBoxDockerCompose on GitHub. This post is the short version: what I wired up, how I install on Proxmox when compose is not the right shape, and where the full port map lives so this page does not become a spreadsheet with SEO. Version française.

item.title: MediaBoxDockerCompose
item.description:
Repository · MIT License

Compose-first homelab media stack: fetch content (torrents and Usenet), route it through *Arr apps, add subtitles where needed, then serve libraries with Plex or Jellyfin, with request UIs and monitoring. Configuration is meant to live under a shared ROOT tree on disk as in the repo’s docker-compose.yml.

Blog: what I run in compose, Proxmox helper-scripts, and where the full wish list lives — MediaBox homelab notes.

item.title: Networking evolution — building a home network lab
item.description: Cloud bills pushed me toward a home lab: old PCs, Docker instead of SaaS where possible, and enough scripting to rebuild after a bad weekend. This post is how that network grew — not a perfect design, but one that taught routing, VPNs, and virtualization by breaking things locally. Version française.
